title: What is known about 1RB1RD_0LC0LB_0RE0LD_1LB0RB_1RF---_0RA0RC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RD_0LC0LB_0RE0LD_1LB0RB_1RF---_0RA0RC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The machine runs a base-7 odometer whose step and carry are proved in Lean for all block lengths; a halt needs F on 1 0 1 (proved in Lean), a misaligned carry sweep. Perturbing the block lengths of a real configuration (even keeping them mod 7) makes it halt, so non-halting depends on the arithmetic of the lengths; what happens when a block runs out is described from simulation only.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 108,456 cells have been visited and 36,152 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.446). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.095).

claims.title: No halt in 2·10<sup>10</sup> steps
claims.text: Direct simulation (c/sim.c) from blank tape; at step 14,815,726,146 the right end of the tape reads [16808] 1 [3866] 1 [75891] 1 [16323] 1 [384] 1 [380], with [k] = (010)^k.

claims.title: No halt in the first 1.24×10<sup>19</sup> steps (exact macro run)
claims.text: A macro simulator (blocks of 6 cells, long runs of equal blocks crossed in one go; exact: every macro step is a run of the machine, counted step for step) ran from blank tape to step 12,428,929,969,419,733,536 without a halt. At this block size it gives the same state, head position and tape as the direct simulator after 2,000,010,402 steps. This is a bounded run and says nothing about later steps.

claims.title: The odometer step
claims.text: At the left end the tape is B> [x] M_d [y] … ([k] = (010)k) with markers M0..M6 = 0, 001, 00110, 0010001, 0[2]10, 00101, 0011. One visit moves the first marker from M_d to M_(d+1), adds a copy to [x] and changes the next block by −1, −1, −1, −1, +1, 0 (d = 0..5), for every x, y and any tape beyond.

claims.title: The carry
claims.text: From M6 the first marker returns to M0 with its block +1 and the next marker moves from M_e to M_(e+1) with its block changed as in the step (e = 0..5), for all lengths.

claims.title: A halt needs F on 1 0 1
claims.text: Two steps before any halt the head is in state F on 1 0 1, three steps before in E on 0 1 0 1: the sweep C0 E0 F1 … that carries the odometer meets 0 1 where a well-formed marker gives 0 0.

claims.title: Overflow and run-out events
claims.text: When all digits are 6 the carry reaches the right end, all markers become 0 and a new lowest digit is put in front. When a block gets below about 4 it merges with its marker into longer words and a partial reset puts a new digit in front and merges blocks (examples in the README).

claims.title: Non-halting depends on the block lengths
claims.text: Replacing the block lengths (those ≥ 5) of the real configuration at step 299,991,864 by random lengths in [5, 300] makes the machine halt in 19 of 100 trials within 2·10<sup>7</sup> steps, and in 6 of 300 when every length keeps its residue mod 7. No closed tape language that forgets the lengths (window CTL, or mod-7 run tokens) can prove non-halting.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The rule when a block runs out is not decoded, so halting is not yet a question about a map; it would need a block to run out in a wrong phase (for instance while the next digit is 6).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. The machine runs a base-7 odometer: markers between blocks of 010 are its digits, each cycling through seven shapes, and every change of shape is paid for by the block after it. A halt needs a block to run out at the wrong moment.

facts.text: Steps simulated from blank tape without a halt.
The odometer step and carry, proved in Lean for all block lengths.
What a halt needs, two steps before (Lean).
Even keeping lengths mod 7: the numbers matter.

sections.heading: An odometer in base 7
html: Write [k] for k copies of 010. At each visit of the left end the tape is blocks with short markers between them, and each marker is one of seven words, a digit:

Each visit adds one to the odometer: the first marker moves to its next shape, the block after it changes as in the table and the first block grows by one. A 6 goes back to 0 and carries into the next marker. Lean proves these steps for every block length. Over a full turn of a digit its block loses 2.

When every digit is 6 the carry runs to the right end, all markers become 0 and a new lowest digit is put in front; that is the slow, logarithmic side of the tape. When a block gets too small to pay, it merges with its marker into longer words and a partial reset merges blocks; that rule is not decoded yet.

sections.heading: A carry sweep out of step
html: The machine stops only on E reading 1. E is entered only from C on a 0 moving right; C from B (which has just written the 0 E will read) or from F on a 1. So two steps before a halt the head is in F on 1 0 1 (proved in Lean). The chain C0 E0 F1 C0 E0 F1 … is the sweep that carries the odometer rightwards over 001 001 …; it halts only if it meets 0 1 where a well-formed marker gives 0 0.

Does the shape of the tape alone rule that out? No: when the block lengths of a real configuration are replaced by random ones, about one run in five halts, and still one in fifty when every length keeps its residue mod 7. In those runs a block runs out at the wrong moment (for instance while the next digit is 6) and leaves a malformed marker. The real run never does, so a proof has to follow the actual lengths.

sections.heading: When a block runs out
html: When the second block is used up, the first block resets and the cost moves a level to the right. Some of the reset moments:
2403 = 7⁴ + 2 and 16809 = 7⁵ + 2. At the far right the last block drops by 3 at each rare visit of the right end (380 at step 1.5·1010). The exact carry rule has not been written down.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.446). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.095).
After 109 steps the tape spans 108,456 cells (62,846 left of the start, 86 right), with a density of 1s of 0.333.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A base-7 odometer: markers between blocks of 010 cycle through seven shapes, each change paid by the next block; the step and carry are proved in Lean, the rule when a block runs out is not decoded, and non-halting depends on the block lengths.
